label: Fundamental Groups and Coverings of Small Categories
notes: This appendix runs from printed page 573 to 583 and builds the combinatorial machinery behind complexes of groups. We treat a small category, especially a scwol, as a space: realize it, walk paths in it, divide paths by homotopy, and read off a fundamental group whose covering theory mirrors classical topology.

label: Small Categories and scwols
notes: Recall that a small category has a set of objects and a set of morphisms with associative composition and identities. A scwol is a small category without loops: no nonidentity morphism is invertible and no nonidentity endomorphisms exist, so composable arrows strictly increase a partial order on objects. This loop-free condition keeps the geometric realization a genuine simplicial-type complex.

label: Geometric Realization
notes: The geometric realization turns the category into a topological space. Objects become vertices, morphisms become edges, and each composable pair becomes a triangle filling in the relation. Chains of length k give k-simplices. For a scwol the realization is a piecewise Euclidean complex, and homotopy questions about the category become honest questions about this space.

label: Paths in a Category
notes: A combinatorial path is an alternating word of arrows traversed forwards or backwards, with consecutive endpoints matching. Reversing an arrow is allowed even though it is not a morphism, which is exactly how we build groupoid-like inverses. Concatenation of paths is partial composition. These edge-paths are the discrete loops we will divide by homotopy.

label: Homotopy of Paths
notes: Two paths are homotopic under the equivalence generated by three moves: cancel an arrow against its formal reverse, and replace a composite arrow by the two factors that compose to it, in either order. Each move corresponds to sliding across a triangle of the realization. Homotopy classes of edge-paths are the morphisms of the fundamental groupoid.

label: The Fundamental Group
notes: Fix a base object sigma zero. The fundamental group pi_1 of the category at that base is the group of homotopy classes of closed edge-paths beginning and ending there, with concatenation as product. For a connected category the choice of base only changes pi_1 up to isomorphism, exactly as in the topological setting it generalizes.

label: Coverings of Small Categories
notes: A covering is a functor from a category onto our base category that is a local isomorphism: over each object it restricts to a bijection between the arrows entering or leaving the fibers. Locally it looks like a disjoint union of copies of stars. This is the categorical translation of an unramified covering space and it lifts paths uniquely.

label: Path Lifting and Monodromy
notes: Unique path lifting holds: given a path downstairs and a start point in the fiber, there is exactly one lift. A closed path therefore permutes the fiber over the base object, giving the monodromy action. The fundamental group acts on the fiber, and for the universal cover that action is simply transitive and free.

label: The Galois Correspondence
notes: Connected coverings of a connected category, up to isomorphism, correspond to conjugacy classes of subgroups of pi_1. The subgroup is the image of the covering's fundamental group; normal subgroups give regular coverings whose deck group is the quotient. The trivial subgroup yields the universal cover, the top of the lattice.

label: The Universal Cover
notes: The universal cover is the simply connected covering on which pi_1 acts freely with quotient the original category. Its objects are homotopy classes of paths out of the base. This is the object that carries the fundamental group's action and makes the cover a tree-like or developable space when the category is a scwol.

label: Why This Builds Complexes of Groups
notes: A complex of groups is, up to development, a scwol with a fundamental group and an action on its universal cover. The local groups are the stabilizers, the universal cover is the development, and developability means the action recovers the geometry. The covering theory of this appendix is precisely the engine for that construction.

label: Recap and Outlook
notes: We realized a small category, defined edge-paths and their homotopy, extracted pi_1 at a base object, and built coverings governed by a Galois correspondence with the universal cover at the top. Carrying a pi_1 action on its universal cover, a scwol becomes the backbone of the complex-of-groups theory that follows.
